paragraphs: Summit Therapeutics Inc. ("we", "Summit" or the "Company") is a biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of patient-, physician-, caregiver- and societal-friendly medicinal therapies intended to improve quality of life, increase potential duration of life, and resolve serious unmet medical needs. The Company's pipeline of product candidates is designed with the goal to become the patient-friendly, new-era standard-of-care medicines, in the therapeutic area of oncology.

The Company's current lead development candidate is ivonescimab, a novel, potential first-in-class bispecific antibody intending to combine the effects of immunotherapy via a blockade of PD-1 with the anti-angiogenesis effects of an anti-VEGF (as defined in Part I, Item I Business, Company Overview, Ivonescimab) compound into a single molecule. On December 5, 2022, the Company entered into the License Agreement with Akeso, Inc. and its affiliates (collectively, "Akeso") pursuant to which the Company has in-licensed intellectual property rights related to ivonescimab (as amended, the "License Agreement"). Through the License Agreement, the Company obtained the rights to develop and commercialize ivonescimab in the United States, Canada, Europe, and Japan. The License Agreement and transaction closed in January 2023 following customary waiting periods. On June 3, 2024, the Company entered into the Second Amendment with Akeso to expand its territories covered under the License Agreement to also include Latin America, including Mexico and all countries in Central America and South America, the Middle East and Africa. The Company's operations are focused on the development of ivonescimab and other future activities, as the Company determines.
The Company is developing ivonescimab in non-small cell lung cancer ("NSCLC") and colorectal cancer ("CRC"), specifically conducting Phase III clinical trials in the following proposed indications:

(a) ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy in patients with epidermal growth factor receptor ("EGFR")-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC who were previously treated with a third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor ("TKI") ("HARMONi");

(b) ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC (including separate statistical analyses planned for patients with squamous NSCLC and non-squamous NSCLC) ("HARMONi-3");
(c) ivonescimab monotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC whose tumors have high PD-L1 expression ("HARMONi-7"); and
(d) ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy in patients with first-line unresectable metastatic CRC ("HARMONi-GI3").

In October 2024, the Company completed enrollment in its HARMONi clinical trial. In May 2025, we announced topline results from our multiregional, double-blinded, placebo-controlled, Phase III study HARMONi. At the prespecified primary data analysis, ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in progression free survival ("PFS"), the magnitude of which we believe to be clinically meaningful, with a hazard ratio of 0.52 (95% CI: 0.41 – 0.66; p<0.00001) compared to placebo in combination with chemotherapy; median PFS was 6.8 months for those patients receiving ivonescimab plus chemotherapy compared to 4.4 months for those receiving chemotherapy. PFS was assessed by blinded independent central radiology committee ("BICR").

We believe the PFS hazard ratio that was observed in both Asian and Western sub-populations to be clinically meaningful. The primary analysis demonstrated the consistency of the magnitude of the PFS benefit between patients randomized in Asian and Western territories, as well as the consistency in a single-region study (HARMONi-A) with this multiregional study.

In a longer-term follow-up of PFS, which included all Western patients and at least six months of follow-up time for all patients, ivonescimab plus chemotherapy demonstrated a consistent improvement in PFS with an observed HR of 0.57 (95% CI: 0.46 – 0.71). With the longer-term follow-up analysis, consistency of the magnitude of PFS benefit was demonstrated between patients randomized in Asia and Western patients when measured by hazard ratio. This longer-term follow-up analysis of PFS was performed at the time of the primary overall survival ("OS") analysis.

Ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy showed a positive trend in OS in the primary analysis without achieving a statistically significant benefit with a hazard ratio of 0.79 (95% CI: 0.62 – 1.01; p=0.057). This trend provides further support for its use in 2L+ EGFRm NSCLC, a setting where high unmet need continues to exist with limited approved options in the United States and other western territories. Currently, there are no FDA-approved regimens that have demonstrated a statistically significant OS benefit in this patient setting. Both Asian and North American patients demonstrated a positive trend in OS. The results of the primary analysis in this multiregional study were consistent with that of the single-region randomized Phase III HARMONi-A study, which demonstrated a statistically significant OS benefit with a hazard ratio of 0.74 in the primary OS analysis in a similar patient population.

In September 2025, an additional ad hoc OS analysis was performed for the HARMONi study whereby the Western patients were followed for a longer period of time (Asian patients were locked at the time of the primary analysis). In this analysis that included longer-term follow-up of Western patients (median follow-up time of Western patients of 13.7 months), a hazard ratio consistent with the primary analysis was observed with an improved nominal p-value (HR=0.78; 95% CI: 0.62 – 0.98; nominal p=0.0332). Median OS for this analysis remained the same in both arms as was observed in the primary analysis. Median OS in Western patients receiving ivonescimab was 17.0 months compared to 14.0 months for those receiving placebo (HR=0.84); median OS in North American patients, specifically, had not yet been reached in the ivonescimab arm compared to 14.0 months in the placebo arm (HR=0.70). The hazard ratios for Western patients in totality, as well as patients from the North American and European regions individually, improved from the primary OS analysis to the analysis with longer-term follow-up of Western patients. Consistent benefit was observed across pre-defined subgroups.
The dual primary endpoints were allocated separate alpha levels and tested individually. The alpha was recycled from the PFS to the OS analysis upon the successful achievement of the PFS endpoint.

Based on the results of the HARMONi clinical trial, we submitted a BLA in the fourth quarter of 2025 to seek approval for ivonescimab plus chemotherapy for this proposed indication. The positive results of the multiregional Phase III study are detailed further under "Product Pipeline" below. As previously disclosed, the FDA noted that a statistically significant overall survival benefit is necessary to support marketing authorization in this setting. After careful consideration of the safety and efficacy profile of the current FDA-approved options for patients in this setting, the positive results of the Phase III multiregional study, including regional consistency, as well as discussions with key opinion leaders and those physicians who have administered ivonescimab to patients in a clinical study setting, we believe that the safety and efficacy data generated in the HARMONi study demonstrates that the ivonescimab regimen offers a potential treatment option for patients impacted by EGFR-mutant NSCLC in this setting with a favorable benefit-risk profile despite the lack of a statistically significant overall survival benefit. Summit announced in January 2026 that the FDA accepted for filing the BLA, seeking approval for ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy for this proposed indication. The FDA noted it intends to perform a complete review of the accepted and filed BLA, including planned mid-cycle and wrap-up meetings, and, subject to major deficiencies not being identified during the FDA's review, proposed labeling, prior to the Prescription Drug User Fee Act goal action date of November 14, 2026.

headings: Risks Related to our Financial Position and Need for Additional Capital
We are a development-stage company and have incurred significant losses since our inception. We expect to incur losses for at least the next several years and may never generate or maintain profits.
We have not yet demonstrated an ability to successfully complete development of any product candidates, which may make it difficult for you to evaluate our success and future viability.
Raising additional capital may cause dilution to our investors, restrict our operations or require us to relinquish rights to our product candidates.
Worldwide economic, social and geopolitical instability could adversely affect our operations, revenue, financial condition, results of operations or ability to raise capital.

We depend heavily on the success of ivonescimab. If we are unable to successfully develop or commercialize ivonescimab, or experience significant delays in doing so, we may continue to incur significant financial losses.
Risks Related to the Development and Commercialization of our Product Candidates
If we experience delays or difficulties in the enrollment of patients in our clinical trials, our receipt of necessary marketing approvals could be delayed or prevented.
Regulatory requirements and timelines may affect the scope and timeline of our trials and the potential market for our product candidates.

If we experience any number of possible unforeseen events in connection with our clinical trials, potential marketing approval or commercialization of our product candidates could be delayed or prevented.
If serious adverse or inappropriate side effects are identified during the development of any product candidate, we may need to abandon or limit our development of that product candidate.
Biologics, such as ivonescimab, carry unique risks and uncertainties that could negatively impact our business.

We may expend our limited resources to pursue a particular product candidate and fail to capitalize on product candidates that may be more profitable or for which there is a greater likelihood of success.
We face substantial competition, which may result in others discovering, developing or commercializing products before us or more successfully than we do.
If we fail to plan, execute and manage our growth effectively, our ability to develop and commercialize products could suffer.
Risks Related to our Dependencies on Third Parties
paragraphs: This section describes certain risks we face in our business. Additional risks we do not yet know of or that we currently believe are immaterial may also impair our business. If any of the events or circumstances described in this section actually occurs, our business, financial condition or operating results could suffer, and the market price of our common stock could decline. In assessing these risks, investors should also refer to the other information contained or incorporated by reference in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and our other filings with the SEC.

We are a development-stage company and we cannot ensure profitability. Since inception, we have incurred significant operating losses. During the year ended December 31, 2025, we incurred a net loss of $1,079.6 million, and cash flows used in operating activities was $322.9 million. As of December 31, 2025 we had an accumulated deficit of $2,294.2 million, cash and cash equivalents of $225.3 million, short-term investments in U.S. treasury securities of $488.2 million, and current and long-term research and development tax credits receivable of $0.9 million. These losses could continue for the next several years as we invest in clinical development of ivonescimab. We expect to continue to generate operating losses for the foreseeable future. Until we can generate substantial revenue and achieve profitability, we will need to raise additional capital to fund ongoing operations and capital needs.

To become and remain profitable, we must succeed in developing and eventually either commercializing or partnering with other organizations to commercialize products that generate significant revenue. This will require us to be successful in a range of challenging activities, including but not limited to completing preclinical testing and clinical trials of our product candidates, discovering additional product candidates, obtaining regulatory approval for these product candidates, and manufacturing, marketing, and selling any products for which we may obtain regulatory approval. We are in the preliminary stages of many of these activities. We may never succeed in these activities and, even if we do, may never generate revenue that is significant enough to achieve profitability.

Because of the numerous risks and uncertainties associated with pharmaceutical products and biological development, we are unable to accurately predict the timing or amount of increased expenses or when, or if, we will be able to achieve profitability.

Even if we do achieve profitability, we may not be able to sustain or increase profitability on a quarterly or annual basis. Our failure to become and remain profitable would depress our value and could impair our ability to raise capital, expand our business, maintain our research and development efforts, diversify our product offerings or even continue our operations.

We have not yet demonstrated an ability to successfully complete development of any product candidates, obtain marketing approvals, manufacture a commercial scale product, or arrange for a third party to do so on our behalf, or conduct sales and marketing activities or otherwise obtain a partner to do so, as is necessary for successful product commercialization. Consequently, any predictions you make about our future success or viability may not be as accurate as they could be if we had a longer operating history.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations is for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared with the year ended December 31, 2024. This comparison should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and related notes appearing elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. This discussion contains forward-looking statements based upon current expectations that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results may differ materially from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of various factors, including those set forth under "Risk Factors" included in Part I, Item 1A or in other parts of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. For a discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations for the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to December 31, 2023, see Part II, Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" included in the 2024 Annual Report on Form 10-K, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on February 24, 2025.

The Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, or MD&A, describes principal factors affecting the results of our operations, financial condition and liquidity, as well as our critical accounting policies and estimates that require significant judgment and thus have the most significant potential impact on our Consolidated Financial Statements. This section provides an analysis of our financial results for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the same period in the prior year.

Investigational Drug 之擴展使用准入
paragraphs: Summit Therapeutics Inc. ("we", "Summit" or the "Company") 為一間生技藥品公司，專注於發現、開發與商業化對患者、醫師、照顧者及社會而言皆為友善的醫療療法，旨在提升生活品質、增加潛在生存時間，並解決嚴重未被滿足的醫療需求。本公司產品候選藥物的研發管道，目標為成為癌症治療領域中對患者友善的新時代標準療法。

本公司目前的主要開發候選藥物為 ivonescimab，為一種新型、具潛力為第一類別的雙特異性抗體，意圖透過 PD-1 的阻斷來發揮免疫治療的效果，並結合 anti-VEGF（如 Part I, Item I Business, Company Overview, Ivonescimab 所定義）化合物的抗血管生成效果，整合至單一分子中。於 2022 年 12 月 5 日，本公司與 Akeso, Inc. 及其關係企業（合稱 "Akeso"）簽訂 License Agreement（如經修正，稱為 "License Agreement"），根據此協議，本公司取得與 ivonescimab 相關的智慧財產權授權。透過 License Agreement，本公司取得在美國、加拿大、歐洲及日本開發與商業化 ivonescimab 的權利。License Agreement 及交易於 2023 年 1 月完成，經過常見的等待期。於 2024 年 6 月 3 日，本公司與 Akeso 籤訂第二修正案，將 License Agreement 覆蓋的地區擴展至拉丁美洲，包括墨西哥及中美洲與南美洲的所有國家，以及中東與非洲。本公司業務聚焦於 ivonescimab 的開發及其他未來活動，如本公司所決定。
本公司正在非小細胞肺癌 ("NSCLC") 與結腸直腸癌 ("CRC") 開發 ivonescimab，並特別進行以下預期適應症的第三期臨牀試驗：
(a) ivonescimab 與化療結合，用於曾接受第三代 EGFR 型酪胺酸 kinase 抑制劑 ("TKI") 治療的表皮生長因子受體 ("EGFR") 突變、局部晚期或轉移性非鱗狀 NSCLC 患者 ("HARMONi");
(b) ivonescimab 與化療結合，用於一線治療的轉移性 NSCLC 患者（包括預計對鱗狀 NSCLC 與非鱗狀 NSCLC 患者進行分離統計分析）("HARMONi-3");
(c) ivonescimab 單獨治療，用於一線治療的轉移性 NSCLC 患者，其腫瘤具有高 PD-L1 表達 ("HARMONi-7"); 以及
(d) ivonescimab 與化療結合，用於一線治療的不可切除轉移性 CRC 患者 ("HARMONi-GI3").

於 2024 年 10 月，本公司完成 HARMONi 臨牀試驗的入組。於 2025 年 5 月，本公司宣佈其多國、雙盲、安慰劑對照、第三期試驗 HARMONi 的初步結果。在預設的主要數據分析中，ivonescimab 與化療結合顯示出統計上顯著的進展自由生存期 ("PFS") 改善，我們認為此改善具有臨牀意義，其風險比為 0.52（95% CI: 0.41 – 0.66；p<0.00001）相比安慰劑與化療組；接受 ivonescimab 加化療的患者中位 PFS 為 6.8 個月，相比接受化療的患者中位 PFS 為 4.4 個月。PFS 由盲測獨立中央放射學委員會 ("BICR") 進行評估。
我們相信在亞洲與西方子羣體中觀察到的PFS風險比值具有臨牀意義。主要分析顯示，在亞洲與西方地區隨機化患者中PFS效益的幅度一致，且與單一地區研究（HARMONi-A）與此多地區研究結果一致。
在較長時間的PFS追蹤中，包含所有西方患者及所有患者至少六個月的追蹤時間，ivonescimab加化療顯示出一致的PFS改善，觀察到的風險比值為0.57（95% CI: 0.46 – 0.71）。透過較長時間的追蹤分析，顯示在亞洲與西方地區隨機化患者中PFS效益的幅度一致，以風險比值衡量。此較長時間的PFS追蹤分析是在主要總體生存（"OS"）分析時進行的。

ivonescimab與化療組合在主要分析中顯示OS有正向趨勢，但未達統計顯著效益，風險比值為0.79（95% CI: 0.62 – 1.01; p=0.057）。此趨勢進一步支持其在2L+ EGFRm NSCLC的應用，此設定中高未滿足需求且美國及其他西方地區的核准選項有限。目前，尚無FDA核准的療法在該患者羣中顯示統計顯著的OS效益。亞洲與北美患者均顯示OS有正向趨勢。此多地區研究的主要分析結果與單一地區隨機化第三期HARMONi-A研究結果一致，該研究在相似患者羣中顯示統計顯著的OS效益，風險比值為0.74。

2025年9月，針對HARMONi研究進行了額外的非預設OS分析，其中西方患者追蹤時間更長（亞洲患者在主要分析時已鎖定）。在包含較長時間追蹤的西方患者（西方患者中位追蹤時間為13.7個月）分析中，觀察到與主要分析一致的風險比值，並改善了名義p值（HR=0.78; 95% CI: 0.62 – 0.98; 名義p=0.0332）。此分析中兩組的中位OS與主要分析結果相同。西方患者接受ivonescimab的中位OS為17.0個月，與接受安慰劑的14.0個月相比（HR=0.84）；北美患者，特別是，ivonescimab組的中位OS尚未達到，與安慰劑組的14.0個月相比（HR=0.70）。西方患者整體的風險比值，以及北美與歐洲地區患者的風險比值，均從主要OS分析改善至包含較長時間追蹤的西方患者分析。預定子羣組中觀察到一致的效益。
雙重主要終點分配了不同的alpha值並分別進行測試。在成功達成PFS終點後，alpha值被重新使用於OS分析。

根據HARMONi臨牀試驗的結果，我們於2025年第四季提交了BLA，以尋求核准ivonescimab加化療用於此提案適應症。多地區第三期試驗的正面結果詳見下文"產品開發路線"。如先前披露，FDA指出必須有統計顯著的總體生存效益才能支持此設定的市場核准。經過仔細考慮目前FDA核准選項在該設定中的安全性與有效性，以及多地區第三期試驗的結果，包括地區一致性，以及與關鍵意見領袖及曾於臨牀試驗中給予ivonescimab治療的醫師討論後，我們認為HARMONi試驗產生的安全性與有效性數據顯示，ivonescimab療法在該設定中為EGFR突變NSCLC患者提供了一種潛在治療選項，具有優良的效益風險評估，儘管缺乏統計顯著的總體生存效益。Summit於2026年1月宣佈，FDA已接受BLA申請，尋求核准ivonescimab與化療組合用於此提案適應症。FDA指出將對已接受並提交的BLA進行完整審查，包括預計的中期會議與總結會議，並在FDA審查期間未發現重大缺失的情況下，於處方藥使用者費用法案目標行動日期2026年11月14日前提出預先標籤。

paragraphs: 以下為對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，係針對2025年12月31日財務年度，與2024年12月31日財務年度之比較。此比較應配合本年度10-K表報表所附之合併財務報表及其相關附註一併閱讀。此討論包含基於目前預期之展望性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性。我們實際結果可能因多種因素而與此展望性陳述所預期者有重大差異，包括於第一部分第1A項「風險因素」或本年度10-K表其他部分所列述之因素。有關2024年12月31日財務年度與2023年12月31日財務年度之財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，請參閱2024年度10-K表所附之「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析」，該報告於2025年2月24日提交至證券交易委員會。
「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析」，或簡稱MD&A，說明影響我們營運成果、財務狀況及流動性之主要因素，以及我們需運用重大判斷之關鍵會計政策與會計估計，因此對我們合併財務報表具有最重大潛在影響。本節提供我們2025年12月31日財務年度與前一年度相同期間之財務結果分析。
Summit Therapeutics Inc.（「本公司」、「Summit」或「公司」）為一專注於發現、開發與商業化患者、醫師、照顧者及社會大眾友善之醫療療法之生物科技公司，這些療法旨在提升生活品質、增加潛在生存時間，並解決嚴重未被滿足之醫療需求。本公司產品候選藥物之開發管道設計目標為成為癌症治療領域之患者友善、新時代標準療法。

本公司目前之主要開發候選藥物為ivonescimab，為一新型、具潛力之首創新藥雙特異性單株抗體，旨在將免疫治療之效果透過PD-1阻斷與抗血管生成之抗VEGF化合物效果結合於單一分子中。2022年12月5日，本公司與Akeso簽訂授權協議，根據該協議，本公司取得與ivonescimab相關之智慧財產權授權（經修正後，稱為「授權協議」）。透過該授權協議，本公司取得於美國、加拿大、歐洲與日本開發與商業化ivonescimab之權利。該授權協議與交易於2023年1月完成，經過常見之等待期。2024年6月3日，本公司與Akeso簽訂第二修正案，將授權協議所涵蓋之地區擴展至拉丁美洲，包括墨西哥與中美洲及南美洲所有國家，以及中東與非洲。本公司之營運重點為開發ivonescimab及其他未來活動，視本公司之決定而定。
本公司正在NSCLC與CRC中開發ivonescimab，並特別進行以下擬議適應症之第三期臨牀試驗：
(a) ivonescimab與化療藥物合併使用，用於曾接受第三代EGFR TKI治療之EGFR突變、局部晚期或轉移性非鱗狀NSCLC患者（「HARMONi」）；
(b) ivonescimab與化療藥物合併使用，用於一線治療之轉移性NSCLC患者（包括為鱗狀NSCLC與非鱗狀NSCLC患者分別進行統計分析之計畫）（「HARMONi-3」）；
(c) ivonescimab單獨使用，用於一線治療之轉移性NSCLC患者，其腫瘤具有高PD-L1表達（「HARMONi-7」）；以及
(d) ivonescimab 與化學治療用於第一線無法手術切除之轉移性結腸直腸癌患者 ("HARMONi-GI3")。

2024年10月，本公司完成HARMONi臨牀試驗的入組。2025年5月，我們公佈多國、雙盲、安慰劑對照、第三期試驗HARMONi的初步結果。在預設的主要資料分析中，ivonescimab與化學治療組合顯示出統計上顯著的進步，我們認為其臨牀意義重大，其風險比為0.52（95% CI: 0.41 – 0.66；p<0.00001）相比安慰劑與化學治療組合；接受ivonescimab加化學治療的患者中位無進步生存期為6.8個月，相比接受化學治療的患者中位無進步生存期為4.4個月。無進步生存期由BICR評估。
我們認為在亞洲與西方子羣體中觀察到的無進步生存期風險比具有臨牀意義。主要分析顯示，在亞洲與西方地區隨機化的患者中，無進步生存期的效益幅度一致，且與此多國試驗一致的單一地區試驗（HARMONi-A）也顯示出一致性。
在較長時間的無進步生存期追蹤中，包含所有西方患者且所有患者至少追蹤六個月，ivonescimab加化學治療顯示出與主要無進步生存期分析觀察到的風險比一致，即HR = 0.57；95% CI: 0.46 – 0.71)。透過較長時間的無進步生存期追蹤分析，顯示在亞洲與西方患者中無進步生存期的效益幅度一致，透過風險比衡量。此較長時間的無進步生存期追蹤分析於主要總生存期分析時進行。

ivonescimab與化學治療在主要分析中顯示出總生存期的正面趨勢，但未達到統計上顯著的效益，風險比為0.79（95% CI: 0.62 – 1.01；p=0.057）。此趨勢進一步支持其在EGFRm NSCLC接受TKI治療後的應用，此設定中，美國及其他西方地區的未滿足需求持續存在且治療選擇有限。目前尚無FDA核准的療法在該患者羣體中顯示出統計上顯著的總生存期效益。亞洲與北美患者均顯示出總生存期的正面趨勢。此多國試驗的主要分析結果與單一地區隨機第三期試驗HARMONi-A的結果一致，該試驗在相似患者羣體中顯示出統計上顯著的總生存期效益，風險比為0.74。

2025年9月，對HARMONi試驗進行了額外的非預設總生存期分析，其中西方患者被追蹤更長的時間（亞洲患者在主要分析時即被鎖定）。在包含更長時間追蹤的西方患者（西方患者中位追蹤時間為13.7個月）的分析中，觀察到與主要分析一致的風險比，並改善了名義p值（HR=0.78；95% CI: 0.62 – 0.98；名義p=0.0332）。此分析中兩組的中位總生存期與主要分析中觀察到的相同。西方患者接受ivonescimab的中位總生存期為17.0個月，相比接受安慰劑的患者為14.0個月（HR=0.84）；北美患者，特別是，接受ivonescimab的中位總生存期尚未達到，相比安慰劑組的14.0個月（HR=0.70）。西方患者整體以及來自北美和歐洲地區的患者風險比，從主要總生存期分析改善至包含更長時間追蹤的西方患者的分析。預定子羣體中觀察到一致的效益。

headings: 與本公司財務狀況相關的風險及對額外資金的需求
本公司為一開發階段公司，自設立以來已產生重大虧損。本公司預期將持續虧損至少數年，並可能永遠無法產生或維持獲利。
本公司尚未展現成功完成任何產品候選品開發的能力，這可能使您難以評估本公司的成功與未來可持續性。
籌措額外資金可能導致投資人權益稀釋、限制本公司營運或要求本公司放棄產品候選品的權利。
全球經濟、社會及地緣政治不穩定情況可能對本公司營運、營業收入、財務狀況、營運成果或籌資能力產生不利影響。
本公司高度依賴 ivonescimab 的成功。若本公司無法成功開發或商業化 ivonescimab，或在該過程中遭遇重大延誤，本公司可能持續產生重大財務虧損。
與產品候選品開發及商業化相關的風險
若本公司在臨牀試驗中遭遇患者招募延誤或困難，本公司取得必要市場核准的時間可能延後或無法取得
法規要求及時程可能影響我們試驗的範圍與時程，以及我們產品候選品之潛在市場。
若我們在臨牀試驗、潛在市場批准或產品候選品商業化過程中遭遇任何可能的未預見事件，可能會導致延遲或無法取得市場批准。
若在任何產品候選品的開發過程中發現嚴重不良或不適當的副作用，我們可能需要放棄或限制該產品候選品的開發。
如 ivonescimab 等生物製劑，可能具有獨特的風險與不確定性，可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
我們可能將有限資源用於追求某特定產品候選品，而未能把握其他可能更獲利或成功機率更高的產品候選品。
我們面臨激烈的競爭，可能導致他人在我們之前發現、開發或商業化產品，或其成效優於我們。
若我們未能有效規劃、執行及管理成長，將可能影響我們開發及商業化產品的能力。
與第三方依賴相關之風險
paragraphs: 本節說明我們在業務中所面臨的某些風險。我們可能還會面臨尚未知悉或目前認為不重要的其他風險，這些風險也可能影響我們的業務。若本節所描述的任何事件或情況實際發生，將可能使我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果受損，並導致我們普通股的市場價格下跌。在評估這些風險時，投資人應同時參考本年度10-K表報表中所包含或參考的其他資訊，以及我們向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交的其他申報文件。

要成為並持續獲利，我們必須成功開發並最終自行商業化或與其他機構合作商業化能產生顯著收入的產品。這將需要我們成功完成一系列具有挑戰性的活動，包括但不限於完成我們產品候選品的預臨牀測試與臨牀試驗、發現更多產品候選品、取得這些產品候選品的監管批准，以及製造、行銷與銷售任何我們可能取得監管批准的產品。我們正在許多這些活動的初步階段。我們可能永遠無法成功完成這些活動，即使我們成功了，也可能永遠無法產生足夠的收入以實現獲利。
由於與藥物產品及生物開發相關的眾多風險與不確定性，我們無法準確預測增加費用的時間或金額，或我們何時、是否能實現獲利。
即使我們實現獲利，我們可能無法維持或提高季度或年度的獲利能力。我們未能成為並持續獲利將會降低我們的價值，並可能影響我們籌資能力、擴展業務、維持研究與開發努力、拓展產品組合，甚至繼續營運的能力。
我們尚未證明我們能成功完成任何產品候選品的開發、取得行銷批准、製造商業規模的產品，或安排第三方代表我們進行這些事項，或進行銷售與行銷活動，或取得合作夥伴進行這些事項，這是實現產品商業化所必需的。因此，您對我們未來成功或生存能力所做的預測可能不如我們有更長的營運歷史時那麼準確。
